### Summary

The build is where availability is fixed. A reader who wants to know whether a configuration can be exercised
at all starts here: the option table says what the library contains, the test registration says which ctest
entries exist and under which environment, and the CUDA[^rg-cbca864c2073] gate says which of them a given build enables. Everything
below is read from the CMake sources at the pin ({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}, {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}).

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects compiled features and registered tests; no numerical equation.

**Data.** CMake cache and Torch ABI[^rg-1a294fa62c1d] in; library, header and test registry out.

**Placement.** Configure, generate, compile, register, then execute.

**Activation.** `BUILD_TESTS=ON`, `FULL_TESTS=OFF`, `CUDA=OFF`; other defaults below.

**Guarantee / limits.** A registered or disabled test is not an executed test.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-build-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

| option or cache value | default | effect and coupling |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD_TESTS` | ON | enters the tests subdirectory and enables testing |
| `FULL_TESTS` | OFF | adds the long reference examples and the decomposition cases |
| `BUILD_EXAMPLES` | OFF | no effect: the examples subdirectory is added unconditionally |
| `CUDA` | OFF | enables the CUDA language; with UCX[^rg-26f9940b7475] it needs commux's CUDA sidecar library |
| `NETCDF` | ON | selects the NetCDF output macro |
| `UCX`, `PNETCDF` | ON, OFF on Apple | UCX needs the commux headers and library; PNETCDF[^rg-6b8251efae9e] the parallel NetCDF library |
| `NMASS` | 0 | legacy mass-index offset; a positive value fails the static index assertion |
| `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` | Release | `-O3` release flags, or `-g3` with address and undefined sanitizers in Debug |
| `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` | empty | prepended to `PYTHONPATH` of every Python ctest that imports snapy |
| `KINTERA_DATA_DIR` | unset | when it holds `nasa9.dat`, the tests get a symlink to it |
| `EIGEN`, `FMT`, `GTEST`, `YAML-CPP` | the package call's default | fetched dependencies, read from a cached archive when present |

: Build options at the pin. {#tbl-ch12-build-options}

The CUDA architecture list starts at 60, 61, 70, 75, 80, 86 and 89; a toolkit of version 12 or later adds 90, 12.8
or later adds 120, and 13 or later removes 60, 61 and 70 ({{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}). The C++ ABI definition
`_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI` is taken from the Torch package by a Python probe and added as a compile definition for
every translation unit. The configuration requires kintera at version 2.6.3 or later.

### Derivation

No continuum or discrete equation is selected here. The dependency chain is configure, generate, compile,
register, then execute. `BUILD_TESTS=OFF` stops before registration; a non-CUDA build keeps its CUDA entries
registered and disables them afterwards. These are configuration predicates, not a convergence derivation, and
they are checked as such: check line `[C6]` walks the five stages over all eight combinations of `BUILD_TESTS`,
CUDA and a GPU[^rg-75af0cfce64b] entry, and confirms that the chain is a total order, that registration is reached exactly when
`BUILD_TESTS` is on, and that a GPU entry on a non-CUDA build stops at registration rather than before it
[check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

Build flags act before any mesh or RK[^rg-74d47dcbcd69] stage exists. Test names carry the lower-case build type as a suffix,
written `<b>` in this chapter (`release` for the default build), through the `setup_test` macro of
{{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}; Python tests carry the suffix `_python` through `snapy_add_python_test`, which
also enrols them for the `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` prepend. The import-path probe must run before any numerical
Python evidence is attributed to a checkout.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch12-build-flow
#| fig-cap: "Build options and test registration: labelled boxes show inputs and decisions in evaluation order. This is a configuration or stencil diagram, not measured data."
#| fig-alt: "CMake options; generated definitions; register tests; enable or disable; execute separately."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch12.figures.fig_build_flow import make_fig
make_fig()
```

### Code

**How to use it.** From a source checkout at the pin, with the README prerequisites and kintera 2.6.3 or later
installed, configure a CPU build and inspect its registered tests. The checkout and the Python packages are set up
in [Install and run](#sec-preface-install); with an older kintera, configuration stops with "Could NOT find
Kintera". These are shell commands, not YAML options:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chengcli/snapy && cd snapy && git checkout <pin>
pip install "kintera>=2.6.3"
cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DFULL_TESTS=OFF -DCUDA=OFF \
  -DSNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH="$(pwd)/build/python"
cmake --build build
python -m pip install . --no-deps --target "$(pwd)/build/python"
ctest --test-dir build -N
```

Use the preface build recipe for its complete test configuration; this smaller recipe selects CPU registration only.
The `build/python` directory must contain the extension built from this checkout before running Python ctests.
`-N` lists tests; it does not execute them. Set `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` at configure time when testing a Python
extension from that build. Missing dependencies can stop configuration; a failed Torch ABI probe reports
"Failed to detect Torch GLIBCXX ABI". YAML cannot change an already compiled feature.

**Checks for a proposed change.** The pinned source's workflow ({{< code .github/workflows/ci.yml >}})
runs pre-commit first, then Release builds and tests on Linux and macOS for changes targeting `main`.
Both configure `BUILD_TESTS=ON`, `FULL_TESTS=OFF`, `CUDA=OFF` and `NETCDF=ON`, install the built Python
package and set `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` to its installation directory. The test commands are:

```bash
# Linux, from build/tests: all enabled registered tests except this decomposition case
ctest --output-on-failure -E '^test_shallow_xy_decomp$'
# macOS, from build/tests: the selected C++ tests and Python import-path probe
ctest --output-on-failure \
  -R '^(test_(eos|plm|gloo_one_tensor)\.release|test_python_import_path_python)$'
```

The macOS build targets are `test_eos.release`, `test_plm.release` and `test_gloo_one_tensor.release`.
Use these workflow selections to reproduce the automated checks; `ctest -N` alone is not a pass.
For the registered test inventory and each test's purpose, see @sec-appc.
**Not provided:** a mandatory pre-submission test policy or the server's required-check settings. The
pinned workflow specifies what runs when a change is proposed, but does not encode branch protection or
a requirement to run every test locally before submitting. In particular, its proposed-change jobs do not
enable `FULL_TESTS` or CUDA; those suites must not be presented as mandatory on the evidence of this file.

{{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} contains this selection step:

```cmake
option(BUILD_TESTS "Build tests" ON)
option(FULL_TESTS "Include additional reference and decomposition tests" OFF)
option(BUILD_EXAMPLES "Build examples" OFF)
option(CUDA "Enable CUDA support" OFF)
option(NETCDF "Build with netcdf support" ON)
```

`BUILD_TESTS` controls the registration stage of `[C6]`; `CUDA` controls compiled CUDA support, not whether
a registered arm has executed. The option defaults precede all runtime choices.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| options | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `BUILD_TESTS` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| build type | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| architectures | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| abi | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| examples | {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}} | `BUILD_EXAMPLES` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| params | {{< code cmake/parameters.cmake >}} | `NMASS` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| indices | {{< code src/snap.h >}} | `static_assert` | `NMASS` |
| packages | {{< code cmake/macros/macro_add_package.cmake >}} | `add_package` | `cmake -DNAME=value` |
| ucx | {{< code cmake/ucx.cmake >}} | `COMMUX_INCLUDE_DIR` | `UCX` |
| sidecar | {{< code src/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `COMMUX_CUDA_FOUND` | `CUDA` |

| cuda gate | {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}} | `SNAPY_BUILD_CUDA` | `CUDA` |

: Implementation sites for the build options. {#tbl-ch12-build-code}

1. Read the options and the build type, probe the Torch ABI, and set the CUDA architecture list from the
   toolkit version. The anchor `BUILD_TESTS` is in {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}.
2. Generate `configure.h`, add the sources, and enter the tests subdirectory when `BUILD_TESTS` is on. The
   anchor `BUILD_EXAMPLES` is in {{< code CMakeLists.txt >}}, where the examples subdirectory is added
   unconditionally.
3. Register the tests with their environment; on a non-CUDA build mark every entry `SNAPY_BUILD_CUDA=0` and
   disable the CUDA-labelled ones. The anchor `SNAPY_BUILD_CUDA` is in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_python_import_path_python` | snapy is imported from under the cache path; the caller's `PYTHONPATH` entry is kept | exact path equality; skip 125 when the path is unset | the script's `assert` statements |
| `configuration_check.py` `[C6]` (report check) | the ordered build and registration predicates | exact symbolic or Boolean equality | the independent check |

: Source assertions, not new solver measurements. {#tbl-ch12-build-tests}

The assertions are the top-level `assert` statements of {{< code tests/test_python_import_path.py >}}; the
registration with `SKIP_RETURN_CODE 125` is in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

No snapy runtime test is executed for this chapter. CUDA and multi-rank entries describe registration only.
The independent checks and their outputs are catalogued in @sec-ch15-ch12-tests.

The independent report check verifies the ordered build and registration predicates in `[C6]`.[^ch12-build-run]
It models the stated contract; it does not execute the compiled solver.

    run: `python src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, CPU, one process;
    Python 3.12.10, numpy 2.5.4, sympy 1.14.0]. Exact symbolic and Boolean assertions; no floating-point tolerance.
    Output `configuration_check.out`, `[C6]`; reproduced for this edit. Solver CTests are source-inspected only.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
No configure or build was run for this chapter. `BUILD_EXAMPLES`, a positive `NMASS` and `NETCDF=OFF` have no
dedicated test. Build compatibility of a given Torch, package and toolchain combination needs a configure smoke
test on that machine.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
